about: Hand-written pairs of DISTINCT defects on the same lines (every pair is two different defects by its reading), to measure what the restatement confirmation merges that it should not. Synthetic: they estimate a rate, they are not data from reviews. Scored with resemblanceOver over the PR 229 ledger of the fit pairs plus the pair (the corpus of the reviewer's measurement) and run through matchRestatements, with the pair citing med/a02.js:40-44.

sets.name: A
sets.about: written by the reviewer of PR 299 (second review round): two distinct defects on the same lines, written to share vocabulary; no claim names a code identifier

pairs.label: test-missing-error-path
pairs.a: the test asserts the cache returns a value but never runs the error path when the file is missing so a broken lookup passes
pairs.b: the test passes because the mock returns undefined and the assertion compares the value against undefined so a broken lookup passes too

pairs.label: stream-drop-vs-retry
pairs.a: the handler drops the response when the stream closes early so the client waits forever for the final frame of the stream
pairs.b: the handler retries the request when the stream closes early so the client receives the final frame twice from the stream

pairs.label: parser-empty-vs-newline
pairs.a: the parser accepts an empty string for the version field so the release tag is written without any version number at all
pairs.b: the parser rejects the version field when it has a trailing newline so valid release files fail with a parse error at load

pairs.label: loop-empty-vs-bound
pairs.a: the loop never terminates when the queue is empty because the condition reads the wrong variable and the worker spins forever
pairs.b: the loop skips the last element when the queue holds one item because the bound subtracts one from the length of the queue

pairs.label: lock-release-vs-double
pairs.a: the lock is released before the write completes so a concurrent reader sees a partially written file and the cache serves stale data
pairs.b: the lock is acquired twice on the same path so the second acquire blocks forever and the cache write never happens at all

pairs.label: regex-dash-vs-bare-path
pairs.a: the regex for the anchor does not match an en dash range so the citation is read as one line and the overlap with the finding is missed
pairs.b: the regex for the anchor matches a bare path with no line number so the citation names a file and line that do not exist anywhere

pairs.label: timeout-zero-vs-whole-run
pairs.a: the timeout is set to zero seconds so the subprocess is killed before the first response arrives and the run reports a false error
pairs.b: the timeout is applied to the whole run instead of each call so one slow verifier ends the run while the other calls still finish

pairs.label: count-wrong-vs-unawaited
pairs.a: the test asserts the count is three but the fixture now holds four restatements so the suite fails for the wrong reason at the count
pairs.b: the test asserts the count is three and the fixture holds three but the assertion never runs because the promise is not returned

pairs.label: severity-text-vs-count-text
pairs.a: the gate names the Critical finding as Important in the blocker text so an operator reads the wrong severity for the open finding
pairs.b: the gate omits the restated count from the blocker text so an operator cannot see which reviewers raised the same open finding

pairs.label: carried-flag-vs-verdict-drop
pairs.a: the ledger stores the restatement before the verdict is read so the carried flag is set on a finding that was never verified
pairs.b: the ledger drops the verdict when a restatement arrives so the finding is verified again as a new candidate instead of carried

sets.name: B
sets.about: written for the fix round: two distinct defects in one function, each claim naming it in the plain way a reviewer writes it

pairs.label: cacheKey: tenant vs case
pairs.a: `cacheKey(resource)` leaves out the tenant id, so two tenants asking for the same resource share one cache entry and the second tenant is served the first tenant's data.
pairs.b: `cacheKey(resource)` lowercases the resource name, so `Report` and `report` collide on one cache entry and the wrong document is served from the cache.

pairs.label: readManifest: bom vs size
pairs.a: `readManifest` returns null for a manifest that starts with a byte order mark, so the adapter is skipped without a message and never discovered.
pairs.b: `readManifest` throws on a manifest larger than one megabyte, so discovery of the whole directory aborts instead of skipping that one adapter.

pairs.label: parseVersion: empty vs newline
pairs.a: `parseVersion` accepts an empty string and returns zero, so a release without a version field is tagged 0.0.0 and published.
pairs.b: `parseVersion` rejects a trailing newline, so a valid VERSION file written by an editor fails to parse at load.

pairs.label: acquireLock: early release vs double
pairs.a: `acquireLock` releases the lock before the write completes, so a concurrent reader sees a partly written file.
pairs.b: `acquireLock` is called twice on the same path, so the second call blocks forever and the write never happens.

pairs.label: retryCall: no backoff vs duplicate
pairs.a: `retryCall` never backs off, so a host that is down is called in a tight loop until the attempt limit is reached.
pairs.b: `retryCall` retries a request the server already accepted, so one slow response makes the call run twice on the server.

pairs.label: buildBrief: truncation vs name
pairs.a: `buildBrief` truncates the claim at eighty characters, so a verifier is briefed with half of a sentence and judges the wrong claim.
pairs.b: `buildBrief` includes the reviewer's name in the brief, so the verifier can tell who raised the finding and is no longer independent.

pairs.label: stampLedger: early stamp vs dropped list
pairs.a: `stampLedger` stamps a carried finding with the new head before the verdict is read, so a finding that was never verified shows as carried.
pairs.b: `stampLedger` drops the `restatedBy` list when it copies an entry, so the restatement is lost from the ledger on the next round.

pairs.label: deriveCleared: reformat vs processes
pairs.a: `deriveCleared` clears a finding whose cited line was only reformatted, so a defect that is still there is marked fixed.
pairs.b: `deriveCleared` shells out to git once per finding, so a ledger of fifty findings starts fifty processes and the round slows down.

pairs.label: tallyVotes: abstain vs unassigned
pairs.a: `tallyVotes` counts an abstain as a real vote, so two abstains and one real settle a finding as present.
pairs.b: `tallyVotes` ignores a vote for a candidate that was not assigned to the verifier and does not say so in its answer.

pairs.label: gradeCoverage: short list vs order
pairs.a: `gradeCoverage` reports a slice as reviewed when its reviewer listed fewer paths than it was given, so an unread path is graded as read.
pairs.b: `gradeCoverage` sorts the unreviewed slices by name, so the order of the answer changes between two runs of the same review.
